subject.title: [Bug]: web_fetch reports exact-size responses as truncated

question: Should OpenClaw define an exact-cap bounded-reader contract for `readResponseText`, and if so should the fix use content-length, a bounded overread/timeout, or require a real failing `web_fetch` response first?
rationale: A repository member already rejected the standalone inference tweak without an explicit content-length/overread contract or real failing-response proof, so automation should not pick the permanent behavior shape.

options.title: Require Contract Then Fix
options.body: Keep this issue open as canonical, require the bounded overread/content-length behavior to be named, then accept a focused helper fix with proof.

options.title: Accept Source-Level Fix Now
options.body: Treat the source-level exact-limit proof as sufficient and allow a narrow `readResponseText` fix after normal review.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Declare exact-cap completion detection outside the current product contract and close the issue until a real user-facing response proves impact.

recommendation.title: Require Contract Then Fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as canonical, require the bounded overread/content-length behavior to be named, then accept a focused helper fix with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This account provided the same-cluster member decision requiring an explicit contract/proof before standalone exact-limit fixes proceed.
